transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Could you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. Um, I hope I'm in the right place for this, and I really don't want to waste your time... I know you deal with much more serious things. 

But, I guess what finally pushed me to come in is... well, it's my shoulders and my neck. They just stay completely clenched all day. It's, um, it's sort of like I'm bracing for a classroom observation that just never ends. I teach preschool, so I know I should be better at managing stress, right? But lately, by the time evening rolls around, my jaw aches so badly I can hardly even enjoy playing my guitar anymore. 

I'm sorry, I know complaining about a sore jaw probably sounds a bit silly, but it's just been really wearing me down. Does that make sense? Am I explaining that okay?
Can you tell me more about the stress or anxiety you're feeling throughout the day, especially in relation to your job as a preschool teacher?

Well, um... I really hope this doesn't make me sound like a terrible teacher, because I promise I care so much about the kids. But my mind just... it keeps circling, I guess. I try to keep it under control, but if I make even a small mistake in, say, a story-time activity, my brain just runs away with it. I start thinking that it means I shouldn't even be trusted with children anymore. 

Which I know sounds extreme... I'm sure other teachers don't overreact like that, right? 

But I just can't stop the thoughts once they start. I start worrying whether I've completely ruined my reputation with the parents. And then, at my age, it just spirals into wondering whether I'll ever get hired again if they let me go, and whether my whole retirement is just slipping away. 

I know I'm probably blowing things way out of proportion, and I'm sorry if this sounds like I'm just complaining. Does that... I mean, is it okay that I'm sharing this? I just really don't want you to think I'm incompetent at my job.
Do you find that these worrying thoughts come up even when there’s no immediate reason to be concerned, and do they feel hard to stop once they start?

Um, yes, I... I suppose they do. Even when things are perfectly fine, they just sort of creep in. I really try my best to manage it, I promise I do. I'll tell myself to just make a list, or I'll say a quick prayer, or try to get out and weed the garden... just anything to focus on the next practical step, you know? 

But it's like... well, it's like one worry just hands off to another. Before I know it, I've lost half the afternoon just sitting there, worrying about things that haven't even happened. I know I should be stronger than that, and I'm really trying to be. I hope that doesn't make me sound too weak or... or unhinged? I just find it really hard to turn it off once it gets going. Is that... is that something you hear from other people, or is it just me?
When you're feeling stressed or anxious, do you notice any other physical symptoms besides the tightness in your neck, shoulders, and jaw?

Well, um... I guess there is one other thing. I really don't want to make a big deal out of it, because I know everyone has trouble sleeping sometimes, right? It's perfectly normal. But, um... I suppose my sleep hasn't been the best lately. 

Most nights, I just... I lie there in bed, and my brain just keeps going. I end up replaying things—like answers I gave in old interviews, or thinking about bills, or those endless licensing forms for the preschool. I can lie there for hours just going over it all. And even when I finally do manage to drift off, I almost always wake up around four in the morning. And the moment my eyes open, I'm already completely tense, just... calculating everything that could possibly go wrong that day. 

I know I should probably try harder to practice good sleep hygiene, and I'm really trying not to let it affect my mood at work. I hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm just falling apart. Is it... is it okay that I'm struggling with this? Do you think that's a normal reaction to stress?
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried about many different things throughout the day, even when there isn’t a clear reason to be concerned?

Um, yes, I... I suppose I do. Like I sort of touched on earlier—and I'm sorry to repeat myself, I just want to make sure I'm answering you properly—my mind really does just keep circling around all sorts of different things. 

It just jumps from one thing to the next. I'll go from worrying if I've completely ruined my reputation with the parents, to suddenly stressing over whether my whole retirement is slipping away. And then, out of nowhere, I'll be agonizing over whether I'll ever get hired again if things go wrong, or... or convincing myself that one tiny mistake in a story-time activity means I shouldn't even be trusted with children anymore. 

I know that probably sounds terrible, and I really do try to keep a positive attitude, especially for the kids. I promise I don't let it show at work. It's just... the worries bounce from one topic to another all day, even when I'm just sitting at home and everything is perfectly fine. Am I... is that the kind of thing you meant? I hope I'm not making it sound like I'm totally incapable of handling everyday life.
Have you been feeling this way—being really worried about different things almost every day—for at least six months now?

Um, yes... yes, it's definitely been at least six months. I, um... I guess if I'm being completely honest, and I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right information... it's been going on for a bit longer than that. 

It started about a year and two months ago. That was, um... well, that was when I was let go from my job at the preschool. I know it's completely normal to be stressed after something like that, right? Anyone would be worried about finding a new job and paying the bills. I just... I thought I would have bounced back by now. I really try not to dwell on it, and I've been applying for things, I promise I have. But the worry just sort of... stuck around since then. I hope it's okay that it's taken me this long to seek help? I just really wanted to try and handle it on my own first.
Do you find that you feel anxious or worried most days, even when nothing specific is happening or when things are going normally?

Well, um... yes. I think it really is most days. Even when things are completely quiet. 

Like I was saying before—and I'm sorry if I'm just repeating myself—even if it's just a normal afternoon at home and absolutely nothing is going wrong, the worry is still just... there. I try really hard to focus on positive things, you know? I'll try to read or organize my old lesson plans so I'm staying productive and not just sitting around feeling sorry for myself. I know I shouldn't let my mind run away with me when everything is perfectly fine. But the anxious feeling just sneaks up on me anyway, no matter how hard I try to push it away and be cheerful. 

Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right. I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining about nothing.
Do you feel like your anxiety or worry is something you can’t really control, even when you try your best to manage it?

Um, yes... I do feel that way. I really do try my best to manage it, I promise I do. I don't just sit there and let it happen if I can help it. 

I'll try telling myself to, you know, just make a list of things to do, or I'll pray, or I'll go outside and weed the garden... just anything to focus on the next practical step and be productive. I know I should be able to just snap out of it and focus on what's in front of me. But it's like... one worry just hands off to another, and before I know it, I've lost half the afternoon to it. 

I feel so foolish admitting that. I should be better at controlling my own thoughts at my age, shouldn't I? I hope you don't think I'm just being weak-willed or lazy when I say I can't stop it. I really am trying. Is that... is that a normal thing to happen when people get stressed?
Have you ever experienced sudden episodes where you feel intense fear or discomfort that comes on quickly and reaches a peak within minutes, like a panic attack?

Um, no... no, I don't think I've ever had anything like that. I've never had a... a panic attack, or anything where it just suddenly hits me all at once like you're describing. 

I mean, I get very worried, obviously, like I was saying. And sometimes my chest feels a little tight when I'm stressing about the bills, but it's not like I'm suddenly terrified out of nowhere or feel like I'm going to pass out. It's more just a... a constant, quiet sort of dread in the background. 

I try to keep myself pretty steady, you know? I wouldn't want to make a scene or anything. I hope that's the right answer? I just want to be sure I'm giving you an accurate picture of what's going on, and I definitely don't want to exaggerate how bad things are. I'm really just dealing with the worrying part, not... not the sudden panic part.

Do you find that your worrying often extends to a wide range of everyday situations, even beyond work, like personal health, family issues, or minor matters such as household chores or running errands?

Well, um... yes, I suppose it does spill over into a lot of different things. I really try not to let it, but... yes. 

My mind just sort of... keeps circling, I guess. I'll start out worrying about whether I'll ever get hired again, which I know is a big thing to worry about, but then it just spirals. I start fretting over whether I've somehow ruined my reputation with the parents from my last school, or if my retirement is just completely slipping away because I'm not working right now. 

And then... well, it even gets into silly things. I almost feel embarrassed saying this, but I'll catch myself agonizing over whether a small mistake I made during a story-time activity three years ago means I shouldn't even be trusted with children anymore. Which is ridiculous, I know it is. I shouldn't be letting my mind go to such extremes over minor things. 

I really try to keep things in perspective, I promise. I don't want you to think I'm completely irrational. Is it... is it common for people to jump from big worries to little ones like that? I just hope I'm not making a bigger deal out of things than I should be.
